doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: Their wedding music
summary: Rowe played at the wedding, with Things Ain't What They Used to Be, an idea borrowed from Gibson's daughter's wedding.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: You got that right. And I enjoyed playing at your wedding.
And just so that everyone knows, your theme song as you walked down the aisle was “Things Ain’t What They Used to Be.”

That’s right. Well you know I got that idea from Dick Gibson’s daughter. When she was married he said I’ll get any group of musicians you want to play for your wedding. So she picked six or seven of the top guys. And they played in a wedding. And I thought now that’s a clever thing to do. That’s where you came in see?
I was in good company then.
Yeah. And that’s what they played when she walked down the aisle.
